name: Match cut pages
what: News pages cut one after another behind you, every 4-6 frames, each a different invented paper and layout (a masthead, a headline in its own typeface, columns of grey text, a picture) - and on every page the same word sits in a red box at the same spot above your head, so the cuts match on it. The pages push in slowly, the last one stays while a band of light crosses the word.
origin: MotionLab's own build after a design in Vibha Ramprakash's claude-video-effects (MIT), 2026-10-28
motion: f0 the first page cuts in (2 f) and the red box pops from 116 % (7 f, slow end with a small overshoot); page k cuts in at 4k + k*k/(pages - 1) - every 4 frames at first, every 6 at the end (pages 10: f0, f4, f8, f13, f18, f23, f28, f33, f39, f45) - and the box punches 2.5 % on each cut (3 f, slow end) in the new page's typeface, its centre locked; the pages push in round the word 5 % over the whole length (slow end); the last page lands at 5 * (pages - 1) (f45) with a 4 % swell (8 f) and a band of light crosses the box f49-f65 (S-curve); the last 5 f it fades (accelerating)
